Maintenance and supply costs constituted 67% of total costs with a third split. This estimated MTV distribution includes approximately 1/3 of costs for administration (35%), 1/3 for marketing (31%), and another 1/3 for maintenance (35%). Because the MTV will be a new platform for the first several years of operation, maintenance and supply costs are expected to be minimal, while marketing needs represent a higher priority to generate initial users. Because costs associated with ownership are incurred regardless of MTV utilization, it will be imperative to identify users in FAU's ownership as early as possible. To estimate FAU's financial risk, Final Technical Report 52/57 only costs associated with maintenance items must be paid to ensure continued availability of the MTV. As estimates are refined during construction and initial ownership, how to mitigate this risk will be evaluated and addressed to ensure continued MTV availability. 14.5 Estimated Cost of Operation The cost of operation is the aggregate costs associated with MTV Modes of Operation 1-4. These relate to user use of the MTV. In addition, planning and regulatory costs may be incurred. These are captured under an Other Activities category. Costs are divided into the following categories: personnel, equipment, materials and supplies, and vendor services (including equipment service contracts). Accurate costs for operation must be individually analyzed and developed for each utilization request with respect to site and CEC. However, some costs can be estimated at this stage when viewed from a daily cost basis rather than from each mode’s total duration (which is not known before developing a test/demonstration plan). Because in-service use of the MTV is likely to be continuous, essential crew and associated user classes are expected to provide 24-hour support (MTV Master and/or MTV Support Personnel). Therefore, additional personnel will be required to establish an on/off-station schedule, especially when operating offshore. Second, traditional 5-day work week/8 hour per day schedules are not a good fit for these activities. Therefore, a 12-hour and 8-hour rate is needed, depending on the mode’s total continuous commitment for personnel. Third, when personnel are away from homeport continuously, shore leave and “sea pay” are common mechanisms to support these situations. Shore leave is a minimum entitlement of 2.5 days for each calendar month of at-sea employment. Sea pay is often a greater wage to compensate for the commitment of serving offshore for long durations and sometimes higher personal risk conditions. Fourth, hourly rates for key at-sea positions have been estimated based on historical data from the R/V Seward Johnson. Costs were divided into fixed and variable types to estimate the daily operation cost. The minimum staffing required in various modes primarily influences fixed costs. Variable costs are likely to be most affected by: • regulatory review, analysis, or monitoring • CEC compatibility with MTV interfaces and capabilities • mooring solution • tow/transport requirements and distances • away port costs These costs can only be developed
